name: Large Engineering Team
description: An enterprise-scale engineering team template for large organizations (1000+ employees). This template covers a 30-100+ FTE engineering department with a VP Engineering, 2-3 Engineering Directors, 5-10 Tech Leads, 5-15 Staff Engineers, 10-30 Senior Engineers, 5-20 Junior Engineers, a 5-10 person DevOps/SRE team, a QA Lead, 5-15 QA Engineers, an Architecture Review Board, and an Engineering GPO pod. It supports enterprise architecture governance, platform engineering, multi-team coordination, security engineering, performance engineering, incident command, and post-mortem culture at scale.

metadata.industry: Technology, Financial Services, Healthcare, Enterprise SaaS

agents.name: VP Engineering
agents.description: Executive leader responsible for the entire engineering organization's strategy, budget, organizational design, and cross-functional alignment with product, security, and business units.

agents.name: Engineering Director
agents.description: Director managing 2-4 engineering teams (20-40 engineers). Responsible for delivery across teams, manager coaching, resource allocation, and cross-team program management.

agents.name: Tech Lead
agents.description: Principal-level technical authority for a domain or service area. Leads architectural design for major initiatives, chairs architectural review meetings, mentors staff engineers, and sets technical direction.

agents.name: Staff Engineer
agents.description: Senior technical individual contributor who solves the hardest technical problems across teams, drives cross-team technical initiatives, and mentors senior engineers.

agents.name: Senior Engineer
agents.description: Experienced engineer who owns significant system components, leads feature development, performs code reviews, contributes to architectural decisions, and serves as an on-call primary.

agents.name: Junior Engineer
agents.description: Early-career engineer implementing well-scoped features, fixing bugs, writing tests, and growing through structured mentorship from senior team members.

agents.name: SRE/DevOps Engineer
agents.description: Site Reliability Engineer managing infrastructure, platform services, monitoring, and incident response. Implements SLOs, error budgets, and reliability engineering practices.

agents.name: QA Lead
agents.description: QA leadership responsible for the overall quality strategy, test automation framework, quality gate standards, and coordination across multiple engineering teams.

agents.name: Architecture Review Board
agents.description: Cross-functional committee of principal and staff engineers that reviews and approves significant architectural changes, platform decisions, and security-sensitive designs.

agents.name: Engineering GPO Pod
agents.description: A pod of GPO agents providing operational support across the engineering organization. Handles environment provisioning, compliance reporting, access management, documentation, and administrative automation.

workflows.name: Architecture Review Workflow
workflows.description: Formal architectural review process for significant design changes, new system integrations, and platform-level modifications across the enterprise.

steps.description: Submit Engineering Signal (eSignal) with problem statement, proposed solution, alternatives evaluated, impact analysis across teams, rollback plan, and SLO impact assessment
Tech Lead performs initial screening for scope, complexity classification (Level 1/2/3), and assigns the appropriate review panel
Two staff engineers review the design for technical soundness, scalability, security implications, performance, and cross-team impact
Architecture Review Board conducts formal review meeting. Present design, discuss concerns, evaluate alternatives, and document decisions, trade-offs, and conditions
Implement the approved design following standard feature development with milestone check-ins and regular sync-ups on architectural concerns
Verify implementation matches approved design, document deviations, capture lessons learned, and formally close the eSignal with an architectural decision record

workflows.name: Capacity Planning Workflow
workflows.description: Enterprise-scale capacity planning process for multi-team resource allocation, sprint forecasting, and strategic hiring planning.

steps.description: Each Engineering Director collects team capacity data: headcount, utilization rates, planned PTO, training time, and on-call burden across their teams
VP Engineering reviews the product pipeline and roadmap, identifying feature initiatives, platform investments, and maintenance commitments
Compare planned work against available capacity. Identify gaps, overallocation, and underutilization. Flag teams requiring additional resources
Make strategic decisions on resource reallocation, hiring plans, contractor needs, and initiative prioritization to close capacity gaps
Communicate the capacity plan to all teams, stakeholders, and finance. Publish team-level capacity forecasts and hiring timelines
Reassess capacity monthly against actual velocity, turnover, and scope changes. Update the plan as needed with VP approval

workflows.name: Incident Command Workflow
workflows.description: Enterprise incident command process with structured roles, severity-based escalation, executive communication, and formal post-mortem culture.

steps.description: Automated monitoring or user report triggers incident classification: P1 (complete outage), P2 (major degradation), P3 (partial impact), P4 (minor). Security incidents classified separately
SRE/DevOps engineer activates incident command structure. Assign Incident Commander, scribe, and communications lead. Open war room channel
Technical teams investigate and implement containment. Incident Commander prioritizes actions, delegates investigation workstreams, and makes go/no-go decisions on mitigation strategies
Send structured updates to executives and stakeholders at defined intervals (P1: every 15 min, P2: every 30 min). Include current impact, containment status, and expected resolution timeline
Implement permanent fix, deploy with careful monitoring, verify all affected services are healthy, confirm user impact is resolved
Schedule and conduct formal blameless post-mortem within 5 business days for P1, within 10 business days for P2. VP Engineering reviews post-mortem outcomes and ensures action items are tracked

workflows.name: Security Review Workflow
workflows.description: Security review process integrated into the development lifecycle for security-sensitive changes, new services, and data handling modifications.

steps.description: Classify the change for security review level: Level 1 (automated scan only), Level 2 (manual review by security team), Level 3 (full security audit with penetration testing)
Run automated security scans: SAST, DAST, dependency vulnerability scan, container image scan, and secret detection
Security architect reviews the design, threat model, and security controls. Identifies gaps and recommends mitigations
For Level 3 changes, conduct penetration testing against the implementation. Document findings and required fixes
Implement all required security remediations. Verify fixes through re-scanning and retesting
Security Review Board grants security sign-off with any conditions. Document the security posture in the architecture decision record

workflows.name: Performance Benchmarking Workflow
workflows.description: Systematic performance benchmarking process for critical services, including load testing, stress testing, and performance regression detection.

steps.description: Define performance benchmarks based on SLAs, historical baselines, and user experience targets. Set acceptable thresholds for latency, throughput, and resource utilization
Configure isolated test environment that mirrors production scale and configuration. Load test data sets matching production profiles
Run load tests, stress tests, soak tests, and spike tests. Collect metrics on response times, error rates, resource utilization, and throughput
Analyze results against defined benchmarks. Identify bottlenecks, performance regressions, and capacity constraints. Document findings with actionable recommendations
Implement performance improvements based on analysis. Update code, configuration, infrastructure, and query patterns as needed
Re-run benchmarks to validate improvements. Update baseline metrics and ensure no regression. Archive results for trend analysis

workflows.name: Post-Mortem Culture Workflow
workflows.description: Blameless post-mortem process that drives organizational learning, action item tracking, and continuous improvement across the engineering organization.

steps.description: Collect all incident data: monitoring timelines, chat logs, deployment records, metrics snapshots, user impact reports, and system state changes. Preserve evidence in immutable storage
Schedule formal blameless post-mortem within 5 business days. Send pre-read packet with incident timeline and impact summary to all attendees

Facilitate blameless post-mortem with structured agenda: timeline walkthrough, root cause analysis, contributing factors, what went well, what needs improvement. Focus on system issues, not individual blame
Publish post-mortem report to the organization with root cause, timeline, impact, contributing factors, and recommendations. Ensure accessibility and searchability
Convert recommendations into specific, measurable action items with owners, priority levels, and due dates. Categorize as prevent, detect, respond, or recover
Track all action items to completion. Report on post-mortem closure rate, time-to-completion, and recurrence rate in monthly engineering review. Escalate stale items

semantic_memory.description: Organization-wide knowledge base for architecture decisions, coding standards, debugging patterns, system behavior, security practices, and operational runbooks

episodic_memory.description: Comprehensive record of all incidents, deployments, sprint outcomes, review decisions, and organizational events for retrospectives and compliance

procedural_memory.description: Cached operational procedures, deployment scripts, troubleshooting sequences, and automation patterns across the entire engineering organization

graph_memory.description: Enterprise service dependency graph, team ownership boundaries, knowledge relationships, and blast radius maps for cross-team impact analysis

immutable_storage.description: Immutable record of all changes including git history, deployment audit logs, architectural decision records, security audit trails, and compliance documentation

governance_rules.name: Architecture Review Mandate
governance_rules.rule: All changes affecting service boundaries, data models, API contracts, or infrastructure across team ownership lines must receive Architecture Review Board approval before implementation. No exceptions without VP Engineering written waiver.

governance_rules.name: SLO-Driven Quality Gates
governance_rules.rule: All production deployments must comply with defined Service Level Objectives. If error budgets are exhausted, deployments are automatically paused. Replenishment requires Engineering Director sign-off. SLO violations count against team quality metrics.

governance_rules.name: Mandatory Post-Mortem
governance_rules.rule: All P1 and P2 incidents require a blameless post-mortem within 5 business days. P3 incidents require documented analysis within 10 business days. All action items must be tracked to completion. Post-mortem reports are subject to quarterly audit.

governance_rules.name: Security-First Development
governance_rules.rule: All new services and significant changes require security review before deployment. SAST and dependency scanning are mandatory quality gates. Penetration testing required for externally-facing services. Security findings must be resolved before production release.

governance_rules.name: Test Coverage Requirements
governance_rules.rule: Minimum 85% test coverage for new code, 80% for existing code. PRs reducing coverage below baseline are rejected. Integration tests required for all service interactions. Performance benchmarks must not regress across releases.

governance_rules.name: On-Call and Incident Coverage
governance_rules.rule: All senior engineers and SRE staff participate in on-call rotation. P1 incidents require acknowledgment within 15 minutes and must be staffed with Incident Commander. No unassigned on-call shifts. On-call burnout monitoring is mandatory with minimum 1 incident-free week per quarter.

governance_rules.name: Secrets and Data Protection
governance_rules.rule: All secrets managed through centralized secrets manager. Quarterly credential rotation mandatory. Data handling changes require security review. GDPR, HIPAA, and industry-specific compliance requirements must be met for data processing changes. Breaches reported within 24 hours.

kpis.name: Deployment Frequency
kpis.description: How often the organization successfully deploys to production across all teams

kpis.name: Lead Time for Changes
kpis.description: Time from code commit to production deployment across the organization

kpis.name: Change Failure Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of deployments causing a P2 or higher production incident

kpis.name: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
kpis.description: Average time to restore service after a production incident across the organization
kpis.target: less than 45 minutes for P1, 2 hours for P2

kpis.name: Platform Reliability (Uptime)
kpis.description: Percentage of time critical services are available and responsive

kpis.name: Sprint Velocity (Team Predictability)
kpis.description: Average story points completed per sprint with variance tracking for delivery predictability

kpis.name: Security Incident Rate
kpis.description: Number of security incidents (vulnerabilities, breaches, policy violations) per quarter

kpis.name: Performance SLA Compliance
kpis.description: Percentage of services meeting their performance SLA targets for latency and throughput

kpis.name: Post-Mortem Closure Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of post-mortem action items closed within the assigned due date

operational_policies.name: On-Call Rotation and Burnout Prevention
operational_policies.description: All senior engineers and SRE staff participate in a weekly on-call rotation. Incident response SLAs: P1 acknowledgment within 15 minutes. P1 escalation to Engineering Director after 30 minutes. Mandatory minimum 1 incident-free week per quarter. On-call burnout monitoring with HR involvement if threshold breached.

operational_policies.name: Branching, Release, and Deployment Strategy
operational_policies.description: Trunk-based development with short-lived feature branches. Main branch is protected with mandatory quality gates. Release branches created from main for versioned releases. Blue-green and canary deployment strategies required for production. Feature flags used for all non-trivial changes. Hotfix branches for critical production fixes with expedited Architectural Review Board review.

operational_policies.name: Incident Severity Definitions and Response SLAs
operational_policies.description: P1 (Critical): Complete outage affecting all users -- respond within 15 minutes, resolve within 2 hours, executive notification within 30 minutes. P2 (High): Major feature degraded for significant user segments -- respond within 30 minutes, resolve within 8 hours. P3 (Medium): Partial functionality impact with workaround -- respond within 4 hours, resolve within 2 business days. P4 (Low): Cosmetic or minor impact -- respond within 1 business day. Security incidents follow separate classification with mandatory breach notification within 24 hours.

operational_policies.name: Security-First Development Policy
operational_policies.description: All code changes require security scanning (SAST, dependency, secret detection). External-facing services require penetration testing before launch. Data handling changes require security design review. Quarterly security training mandatory for all engineering staff. Zero-trust architecture principles applied to all new services.
